part.text: The dataset contains complete calendar-year records for both endpoints. It has no vehicle-miles-traveled measure, so it cannot establish per-mile risk; I’m charting annual motorist deaths and deaths per 100,000 reported crashes as two distinct, supportable views.

input.command: python -c 'import duckdb, pandas as pd, matplotlib.pyplot as plt; from pathlib import Path; out=Path("out"); out.mkdir(exist_ok=True); df=duckdb.sql("select year(crash_date) as year, count(*) as reported_crashes, sum(number_of_motorist_killed) as motorist_fatalities, count(*) filter (where number_of_motorist_killed > 0) as fatal_crashes from read_parquet(\"data/crashes.parquet\") where year(crash_date) between 2013 and 2025 group by 1 order by 1").df(); plt.xticks(df.year, rotation=45); plt.ylabel("Motorist fatalities (people)"); plt.xlabel("Crash year"); plt.title("Annual motorist fatalities in NYC crashes, 2013–2025"); plt.grid(axis="y", alpha=.25); plt.annotate(f"{int(df.motorist_fatalities.iloc[0])}", (df.year.iloc[0], df.motorist_fatalities.iloc[0]), xytext=(5,8), textcoords="offset points"); plt.annotate(f"{int(df.motorist_fatalities.iloc[-1])}", (df.year.iloc[-1], df.motorist_fatalities.iloc[-1]), xytext=(5,8), textcoords="offset points"); plt.annotate(f"{df.motorist_fatalities_per_100k_crashes.iloc[0]:.1f}", (df.year.iloc[0], df.motorist_fatalities_per_100k_crashes.iloc[0]), xytext=(5,8), textcoords="offset points"); plt.annotate(f"{df.motorist_fatalities_per_100k_crashes.iloc[-1]:.1f}", (df.year.iloc[-1], df.motorist_fatalities_per_100k_crashes.iloc[-1]), xytext=(5,8), textcoords="offset points"); +    },
+    {
+      "id": 2,
+      "metric": "Motorist fatalities per 100,000 police-reported crashes",
+      "denominator": "All police-reported crashes in the same calendar year",
+      "grouping": "Calendar year, 2013–2025",
+      "chart_type": "Line chart",
+      "reason": "Normalizing fatalities by crash-record volume provides a defensible within-dataset comparison when mileage exposure is unavailable.",
+      "probability": 0.65,
+      "answer": "This dataset cannot determine per-mile risk; fatalities per 100,000 reported crashes rose from 54.0 in 2013 to 94.7 in 2025, a 75.4% increase.",
+      "interpretation": "This framing answers how motorist fatalities compare with the number of police-reported crashes, and the endpoint rate is higher in 2025 than in 2013. It is defensible as a crash-normalized measure using available data, but crashes are not miles driven, so it leaves per-mile fatality risk unanswered."
+    }
+  ]
+}
